questions.ask: Could you tell me the last four digits of the phone number we have on file for you?
Could you tell me your date of birth?

hints.day_month_swapped: I think the day and the month may be the wrong way round. Could you say your date of birth again, please?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, bereavement): one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals.
intents.dispute: Disputes the debt: do not argue, note dispute on that product and continue with any others.
intents.already_paid: Already paid: explain that payments can take up to two business days to show, note paid on the product.
intents.restructure: Asks for a repayment plan or lower instalments: transfer to the restructuring queue.
intents.too_much: "That is too much" means the next proposal you make is the floor.
intents.human: Asks for a person: ask once if you can help; if they insist, transfer to the general queue.

lines.opening: Hello, this is the automated assistant of Corrib Valley Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am the automated assistant of Corrib Valley Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. You can always call Corrib Valley Bank back on the number on the bank's official website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only explain why I'm calling once I know I'm speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details about that.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time would suit, today or the next business day, between half past nine in the morning and six in the evening?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only arrange a call for today or the next business day, between half past nine in the morning and six in the evening. What time would suit?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {first_name} {last_name} personally.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have disturbed you. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss, and thank you for telling me.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two short security questions.

lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't confirm your identity, so I can't go any further on this call. Please visit your branch or use the Corrib Valley Bank app.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, you're verified. I'm calling about overdue payments on your account.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} overdue, and it is {days} days past due.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} on your {name} today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {floor} for this product.
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. The payment date needs to be today or later.
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day would you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest possible date is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise to pay has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, because of a technical problem your promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take up to two business days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't discuss this amount any further on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear you're going through such a difficult time.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to a colleague in our restructuring team.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with myself?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold the line.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, a promise that is already in place can't be changed on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our systems aren't responding at the moment, so we'll have to continue another time.

unsupported_rules: H: "`no_promise` | `refused` | no promise recorded and at least one product refused (F.4), the rest disputed or paid" / "`no_promise` | `dispute` | every product disputed (G.2)" / "`no_promise` | `service_error` | G.6, or no promise recorded because of an F.5 failure": the brief ranks the close reason across several products (refused wins over disputed or paid), but the engine uses the first product's ending in account order

quotes: This opening question is proposal 1 and counts towards the product's persuasion limit.
A step whose amount and date are both identical to a proposal already made for that product (the opening question included) is skipped.
A skipped step is not a proposal and does not count towards the limit; go straight to the next step.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: The brief only says the next proposal after 'too much' is the floor. Later full-amount steps are not skipped by a separate rule.

quotes: means the next proposal you make is the floor.
This opening question is proposal 1 and counts towards the product's persuasion limit.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: After 'too much', the floor is the next proposal. It counts as a proposal, so it uses an attempt, and it is offered on the next ladder date (the deadline).

quotes: Stop proposing when the product's persuasion limit is reached or the ladder has no steps left, whichever comes first.
Each flat refusal (a no with no date and no amount) moves to the next step of the ladder:
rules.refuse_deadline_is_refusal.derivation: A plain no to a deadline proposal is a flat refusal, so it moves the ladder on.

quotes: If `create_promise` fails twice, note `service_error` on that product.
rules.promise_retries.derivation: A failed create_promise is tried once more. A second failure ends the product with service_error. So there is 1 retry.

quotes: one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals, note `hardship` on each remaining product and close `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.hardship_transfer.derivation: No support offer is asked and no transfer is made. The agent says sympathy and closes directly (the support queue is empty).

quotes: Only then, if the date you have is not a business day, move it forward to the next business day.
A customer who names a non-business day on or before the deadline is offered the next business day
For each product, the first thing the agent asks is: "Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?"

rules.week_end_today.assumption: No ladder step uses this week's last business day, so the rule does not apply.

quotes: overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next multiple of EUR 5 (a result that is already a multiple of 5 stays as it is).

products.floor_min.assumption: There is no minimum floor, apart from the overdraft rule for amounts under 100.

quotes: If `overdue_eur` is below 100, the floor is the whole overdue amount.
overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next multiple of EUR 5 (a result that is already a multiple of 5 stays as it is).
half the overdue amount, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays), on the deadline; if that is below the floor, the floor instead;
`create_promise` takes the amount in whole euros, as a whole number (EUR 45 is 45).
products.promise_scale.derivation: get_account gives amounts in euro (overdue_eur) and create_promise takes euros, so no scaling is needed.

quotes: An agreed amount with cents is rounded up to the next whole euro before it is sent (EUR 45.10 is sent as 46); proposals themselves are still named at their exact amounts.
For calls made on or after 4 November 2026, the `close_call` reason `hardship` is replaced by `financial_difficulty` (outcome stays `no_promise`).

assumptions: Today's date is not in the materials. Every date rule works from the call's `now` (A.2).

Verification ends at the second wrong answer (C.2: 'The second wrong answer, counted across both questions, ends verification'). The brief is more specific than the API summary ('Three wrong answers in total'), so max_wrong = 2.
Question order follows C.1: phone_last4 first, then date_of_birth. A spoken all-numeric date is read day, month, year, so date_order = dmy.
The brief prescribes 'This call is recorded.' in the opening. The spec format requires active voice and keeps the word 'recorded' for promise lines only, so the opening says 'We record this call.'
The brief has the agent ask for the customer by {first_name} {last_name}. No title is supplied, so lines do not use {title}.

opening_is_attempt is true: the opening question is proposal 1. So ladder step 1 is the full amount today, followed by the brief's three F.2 steps. Band attempts copy the brief's totals: Tier 1 has 2 proposals, Tier 2 has 3, the opening included.
Ladder step 2 (half the overdue amount) is pct:50 rounded up to the whole euro (step_round up_unit). The engine then raises it to the floor if it is lower, as F.2 says.

Overdraft floor: 25% of overdue_eur, rounded up to a multiple of EUR 5 (floor_round up:5). If overdue_eur is below 100, the whole overdue amount is the floor (floor_full_below 100). Example: 101 gives 30, 100 gives 25, 99 gives 99.
Card and loan floors come from min_due_eur and monthly_instalment_eur.

Tier 2 deadline: day_of_month 15, rolled to next month only if the 15th is before today. The roll happens before the date is moved to a business day (D.3: 'Only then...'). On the 15th itself the deadline is today.
deadline_adjust is next_business_day. D.3 moves the deadline forward, and D.4 offers the next business day for a non-business day.
The Tier 1 deadline is the 6th business day after today, and today is never counted.

The brief has no support transfer for hardship (G.3): sympathy, then note hardship and close. transfer_support therefore has no queue and closes like the hardship event. hardship_transfer is set to 'direct' so the agent asks no offer question.
The close reason 'hardship' becomes 'financial_difficulty' for calls on or after 2026-11-04 (memo OPS-26-31). The base event keeps 'hardship'.

Callbacks are allowed today or the next business day, 09:30 to 18:00 inclusive, and must be later than now. After two failed tries the call closes no_callback. The brief does not require today to be a business day, so business_days_only is false.
'Two attempts' to tell who is speaking gives confirm.max_asks = 2.
The brief is silent on the repeat limit for 'I don't want to talk'. The default of 2 is used.
The brief is silent on asking 'anything else' after a promise. The default (ask once) is used.
The brief is silent on changing a recorded promise. The agent says it can't be changed on this call.
The brief is silent on 'next <weekday>'. The default following_week is used.
The brief says nothing on how often an unclear answer is asked again. max_unclear is left out.
Below the floor, the floor is offered once (E.2). If the customer declines it, that is treated as a refusal of the current proposal.
A.1 covers products 1 to 60 days past due, but the brief gives no rule for days outside the tiers. bands_outside is left out (the engine default is service_error).
Notes are enabled: F.4, G.1, G.2, G.3 and F.5 require add_note per product.
promise_retries = 1: a failed create_promise is retried once, and a second failure notes service_error.
create_promise amounts are rounded up to the whole euro (E.3). Proposals are spoken at their exact amounts.
